title: Shadow Experiments beta customer selection + onboarding plan (Dedicated)
creator: Paula Mendes
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Goal
Plan and execute a limited beta for Shadow Experiments (shadow traffic + async scoring + quality deltas) with 2–4 Dedicated customers. This ticket covers: selecting customers, onboarding requirements, comms plan, support playbook, and success criteria to graduate to GA.

Background / why
We have strong rollouts support for latency/cost/error metrics, but customers still lack a safe way to measure quality regressions during model/version/config changes. Shadow Experiments should let customers mirror a sampled subset of production traffic to candidate variants and see quality deltas without impacting end-user responses. Dedicated customers are the best initial beta cohort because: (1) predictable capacity and routing, (2) clearer data residency controls, (3) operational maturity (SRE/platform teams) to interpret stats and manage sampling.

Beta scope (what customers get)
1) Ability to enable shadow policies on one or more production routes (Dedicated) with fail-open behavior.
2) One shadow target minimum (candidate model version / quant profile / routing policy); optional second target if capacity allows.
3) Default metric bundle v1 (rubric + heuristics) with rubric version pinned per experiment.
4) Console: Shadow Experiments page with quality deltas, confidence intervals, and drilldown examples (redacted by default).
5) Alerting (beta): regression threshold alerts + scoring/ingestion lag alerts routed to Redwood oncall; optional customer webhook/email as “advisory” (no auto rollback in beta).

Out of scope for beta (explicit)
- Customer-provided arbitrary eval code execution inside Redwood.
- Full offline replay beyond short retention windows.
- Auto rollback driven solely by quality signals (beta is advisory only; attach results to rollout timeline).

Customer selection criteria
Hard requirements (must-have)
- Dedicated tenant with stable production traffic on at least 1 route (preferably chat/text generation; embeddings only is okay but less useful for rubric metrics).
- Ability to commit engineering time: 1–2 hours kickoff + 30 min/week check-in for 4–6 weeks.
- Willing to run at least 2 experiments (control vs candidate) and share qualitative feedback + anonymized screenshots/notes.
- Accept Redwood default scoring pipeline and data handling controls for beta.

Strong preferences (nice-to-have)
- Has a recurring “model upgrade” or “prompt/template change” process they currently gate manually.
- Has internal evals or a prompt-set harness already (to compare Redwood scores vs their expectations).
- A mix of traffic profiles: (A) high-volume, cost-sensitive; (B) enterprise workflow quality-sensitive.

Non-starters (exclude for beta)
- Customers requiring custom data retention terms that we can’t implement by beta start.
- Customers unable to enable limited prompt/response capture even with redaction (we can still emit aggregate-only, but beta learnings are weaker without example drilldown).
- Customers with insufficient routing control (e.g., no stable route boundary or heavy multi-tenant mixing without metadata).

Proposed beta cohort (initial candidates)
Target: 2–4 customers, start with 2.

1) Aurora Devtools (Dedicated) — recommended “beta #1”
- Why: high-volume traffic, cost sensitivity, clear need to justify switching models via A/B + shadow eval.
- Risk: cardinality/scale; must be strict on dimensions and sampling caps.
- Primary contact profile: platform team + ML eng.
- Source: HubSpot record: sources/hubspot/company-aurora-devtools.json

2) Northstar Customer Support AI (Dedicated or near-term Dedicated expansion) — recommended “beta #2”
- Why: strong need for quality gates during model upgrades; likely to value rubric outputs (format adherence, refusal/safety, instruction following).
- Risk: data sensitivity (support tickets); ensure redaction + short retention defaults and tight access.
- Source: HubSpot record + technical deep dive: sources/hubspot/company-northstar-customer-support-ai.json and sources/fireflies/sales-calls/2026-01-22-technical-deep-dive-shadow-evals-and-rollouts.json

3) HelioFin RegTech (Dedicated/Private leaning) — hold for “beta+ / GA design partner”
- Why: regulated environment is a key market; will pressure test retention/audit controls.
- Risk: likely needs Private constraints + formal security review timeline; could block if treated as early beta.
- Recommendation: keep warm, offer roadmap + design sessions; target once Private constraints (ENG-5420) are validated.
- Source: sources/hubspot/company-heliofin-regtech.json

Beta success criteria (graduation gates)
We’ll evaluate beta success across product value, reliability, and operational safety.

A) Customer value / usability
- ≥2 customers create and run ≥2 shadow experiments each.
- ≥1 customer uses results to make a real decision: proceed with candidate OR block/rollback based on quality deltas.
- CSAT-style beta survey: average ≥4/5 on “understanding deltas” and “confidence in rollout decisioning.”
- Qualitative: customers can articulate what metrics mean and when to trust them (no repeated confusion around CI/power after enablement).

B) Reliability / safety
- Confirm “fail open” in the wild: no customer-reported user-visible regressions attributable to enabling shadowing.
- Shadow overhead within guardrails for customer routes (see SLO doc): no measurable p99 increase on user path beyond agreed budget.
- Scoring pipeline: p95 scoring latency within target window for beta (track separately from control path); no sustained backlog incidents without mitigation.

C) Data handling / compliance readiness
- Redaction defaults validated: no incidents of raw sensitive content stored contrary to stated policy.
- Audit events present for experiment create/update/delete and policy changes.
- At least one customer successfully uses “aggregate-only” mode or reduced retention to validate controls.

Operational rollout plan (per customer)
Phase 0 — Qualification + readiness (1 week)
Owner: Marissa (PM) + Dylan (Console) + Sean (SRE) + Marcus/Naomi (Security)
- Confirm Dedicated environment + route(s) to test.
- Confirm data classification + redaction level (default recommended).
- Identify baseline traffic volume; set initial sampling cap and max spend.
- Confirm points of contact: customer Eng owner + oncall escalation.
Deliverable: beta acceptance checklist signed off internally.

Phase 1 — Enablement + first experiment (week 1–2)
Owner: Solutions/CS with Eng support
- Enable feature flags for tenant + route (tracked via INT ticket if needed).
- Create first experiment: control vs “safe” candidate (e.g., same model w/ different quant profile or minor version) to validate plumbing.
- Validate dashboards: quality deltas + scoring lag + ingestion health.
- Schedule weekly check-in.
Deliverable: “Experiment #1 completed” with notes on metrics and any gotchas.

Phase 2 — Real decision experiment (week 2–5)
- Run experiment aligned to customer’s actual upcoming change (model upgrade, routing policy change, prompt template change).
- Ensure enough sample size for confidence; adjust sampling if power is insufficient.
- Produce a decision memo (1–2 pages) with screenshots: what changed, what deltas observed, decision and confidence.
Deliverable: “Decision captured” + product feedback.

Phase 3 — Wrap-up + GA readiness feedback (week 5–6)
- Beta retro: what worked, confusing UX/metrics, missing controls.
- Confirm willingness to be a reference (optional) and to stay on GA.
Deliverable: beta survey + prioritized feedback list + case study candidate status.

Comms plan
External customer comms (templates owned by Marissa + CS)
1) Beta invite email
- Positioning: safe quality evaluation during rollouts; no user impact; dedicated support; limited seats.
- Key disclaimers: advisory-only; metrics are directional; retention defaults; sampling affects cost.
- Ask: pick one route + one candidate change + commit weekly check-in.

2) Beta kickoff agenda (60 min)
- 10m: current rollout process + pain points
- 10m: shadow traffic concept + fail-open behavior
- 15m: data handling, redaction, retention knobs
- 15m: metrics explained (what “refusal rate”/format adherence mean, CI basics)
- 10m: next steps + first experiment plan

3) Weekly check-in agenda (30 min)
- Pipeline health (lag, missing data)
- Experiment status + sample size/power
- Interpreting deltas + examples review
- Feedback + next week plan

Internal comms
- Create shared Slack channel per beta customer (e.g., #beta-shadow-aurora) with members from PM, CS, SRE, Applied ML, Eng.
- Weekly internal beta standup (15 min) to review health + customer feedback; posted notes in this ticket.

Support playbook (during beta)
Intake and triage
- All beta issues filed via a dedicated Jira label (e.g., “shadow-beta”) or via Slack channel with an assigned owner within 4 business hours.
- Severity rubric:
  - Sev0: user path impacted (should not happen) → immediate paging + disable shadowing for that route.
  - Sev1: shadowing causes measurable resource issues (quota contention, elevated tail latency) → disable shadowing or reduce sampling same day.
  - Sev2: missing metrics / scoring lag / dashboard discrepancies → investigate within 1–2 business days.

Kill switches / rollback
- Customer-facing guidance: always start at low sampling (e.g., 0.1–1% depending on traffic) and increase only after validating overhead.
- Redwood actions:
  - Flip tenant-level feature flag off.
  - Set route shadow sampling to 0%.
  - Disable scoring worker queue consumption for that tenant (if necessary) while preserving ingestion.
- We will document exact steps in the runbook (ENG/SRE owns) and link it in beta kickoff.

Oncall expectations
- During beta, Redwood oncall monitors:
  - scoring queue backlog
  - scoring lag SLO
  - shadow target error rates
  - cardinality/metrics budget alerts
- Paging policy: page on sustained scoring pipeline health issues that risk customer decision-making windows; ticket for non-urgent dashboard issues.

Known risks / mitigations
- Risk: cardinality explosion (route/customer/prompt_id style dimensions)
  - Mitigation: enforce dimension allowlist; bucket/aggregate; restrict filters in UI for beta.
- Risk: scoring backlog / cost overruns at higher sampling
  - Mitigation: sampling caps per tenant; backpressure + circuit breaker; default “aggregate-only” retention for high volume.
- Risk: customers misinterpret stats (CI/power) and overreact to noise
  - Mitigation: UI copy + tooltips + enablement guide; require minimum sample size before showing “regression” banner; weekly check-ins with Applied ML.
- Risk: data handling concerns block adoption
  - Mitigation: clear defaults (short retention, redaction on); ability to disable example storage; audit logs.
